Basic ATC

Depart via

An ATC instruction directing the pilot to follow a specified Standard Instrument Departure (SID) or route after takeoff.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Depart via?

In this glossary, Depart via refers to: An ATC instruction directing the pilot to follow a specified Standard Instrument Departure (SID) or route after takeoff.

How is Depart via used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Ground: Delta 789, cleared for takeoff runway 27, depart via the LAM3A departure."

Why does Depart via matter in aviation?

Depart via matters because it supports clear communication in Basic ATC contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Who uses Depart via?

Depart via is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.

What category does Depart via belong to?

In this glossary, Depart via is grouped under Basic ATC. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from ICAO Doc 9432, FAA PCG and published by Protermify Aviation as a static aviation reference page.

Definition

An ATC instruction directing the pilot to follow a specified Standard Instrument Departure (SID) or route after takeoff.

Operational example

Ground: Delta 789, cleared for takeoff runway 27, depart via the LAM3A departure.
